disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated gonococcal infection presenting as isolated septic arthritis of the right third MCP joint
presentation_summary: 18-year-old African American woman with no significant past medical history presented with two days of right dorsal hand pain and swelling, left thumb pain, and bilateral ankle pain.
She denied fever, chills, recent infections, dysuria, skin rashes, bug bites, trauma, and autoimmune family history.
She reported one male sexual partner over the last year and no barrier contraception.
Exam showed significant swelling, erythema, tenderness, and inability to flex digits around the right third MCP joint, plus erythema and tenderness of the left thumb IP joint.
Labs showed WBC 16.05 x10^9/L, ESR 47 mm/hr, and CRP 264 mg/L; right hand MRI showed large third MCP effusion, synovial enhancement, and periarticular edema concerning for septic arthritis.

clinical_course: Discharged with daily home health care for IV ceftriaxone administration.
Advised to notify sexual partner for testing and treatment.
Completed therapy and reported resolution of joint pain and swelling at orthopedic follow-up two weeks later.
quality_warnings: Urine NAAT and blood culture are retained as confirmatory evidence with use_in_ranking false.
The case preserves absent fever, absent rash, and absent dysuria because DGI can present as isolated purulent arthritis.
